text.p: These are the highlights in the Bosnian press on Wednesday. Reuter has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- International donors' conference, expected to raise $1.4 billion for Bosnia's reconstruction, will be held on July 23 and 24 in Brussels, says the office of Haris Silajdzic, a co-president of the Council of Ministers.
- Delegation of the Moslem-Croat federation government visited on Monday Capljina, a Croat-controlled town in southern Bosnia, to compare retail prices of cigarettes and tobacco products.

- The date of the long expected meeting between a chairman of the Bosnia's presidency, Alija Izetbegovic, and Croatian President Franjo Tudjman is still uncertain, but it surely will not happen in next ten days, says a high Bosnian official who asked not to be named.
- Croatian ambassador to Bosnia, Darinko Bago, was very surprised that some Bosnian media have got hold of Croatian draft declaration intended for the Izetbegovic-Tudjman meeting.
- Gerd Vagner, the first deputy High Representative to Bosnia, says the transitional status of Mostar does not provide for joining more municipalities under one administration.
- Joining municipalities opposes Dayton peace accords, says Vagner.
- Bosnian Foreign Minister Jadranko Prlic, currently on an official visit to Slovenia, said that the two countries had signed five agreements.
